name: Paper Cutting
shortcutSummary: Similar to paper folding — track each fold, note where the cut is made, then unfold. The cut appears symmetrically mirrored about each fold line when unfolded.
conceptExplanation: Paper Cutting questions are similar to Paper Folding but involve cutting a shape from the folded paper instead of punching holes. When unfolded, the cut pattern appears symmetrically.

subtopics.name: Paper Cutting — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Paper Cutting questions are similar to Paper Folding but involve cutting a shape from the folded paper instead of punching holes. When unfolded, the cut pattern appears symmetrically.
shortcuts: Cut Shape Tracking: Note the exact shape and position of the cut relative to the fold.
Reverse Unfold Method: Unfold step by step; each unfold mirrors the cut about the fold line.
Edge vs Center Cut: Cuts on the folded edge create connected patterns when unfolded; cuts away from the edge create separate shapes.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A square sheet of paper is folded in half from left to right, then folded in half from top to bottom (folded into 4 layers).
A circular hole is punched in the center of the folded quarter.
How will the paper appear when completely unfolded?
options: Only two circular holes along the central horizontal fold line
A single large circular hole at the center of the sheet
Four circular holes symmetrically distributed, one in each of the four quadrants.
Eight small circular holes arranged in a ring
practiceQuestions.hint: Trace the reverse unfolding steps: each unfold reflects the cut marks across that fold line.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Unfolding the paper twice doubles the cut pattern along both the vertical and horizontal axes of symmetry, producing 1 × 2 × 2 = 4 identical circular holes across all four quadrants.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Count total layers of paper created by the folds (2 folds = 4 layers).
Step 2: Note the location of the cut (center, perimeter, or vertex).
Step 3: Unfold in reverse sequence, reflecting cuts across each fold line to find: Four circular holes symmetrically distributed, one in each of the four quadrants..

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A circular paper is folded in half to form a semicircle, and then folded in half again to form a quadrant (quarter-circle).
A triangular notch is cut on the curved outer edge of the quadrant.
How will the paper appear when completely unfolded?
options: Two triangular notches at opposite ends of the horizontal diameter
A single triangular notch at the top edge of the circle
Six triangular notches arranged unevenly around the perimeter
Four triangular notches evenly spaced at 90-degree intervals along the outer circumference.
practiceQuestions.hint: Trace the reverse unfolding steps: each unfold reflects the cut marks across that fold line.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Since the circular sheet was folded into 4 layers (a quadrant), a single cut on the curved perimeter replicates into 4 symmetrical cuts at 90-degree intervals when fully opened.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Count total layers of paper created by the folds (2 folds = 4 layers).
Step 2: Note the location of the cut (center, perimeter, or vertex).
Step 3: Unfold in reverse sequence, reflecting cuts across each fold line to find: Four triangular notches evenly spaced at 90-degree intervals along the outer circumference..

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A square paper is folded diagonally from bottom-left to top-right to form a triangle, and then folded again along the altitude into a smaller triangle.
Two circular punches are made in the interior of the folded triangle.
How will the paper appear when completely unfolded?
options: Two diamond holes along the main diagonal axis
A single diamond hole centered on the square
Eight circular punches arranged symmetrically in an octagonal pattern around the center.
Eight diamond holes distributed along all four outer edges
practiceQuestions.hint: Trace the reverse unfolding steps: each unfold reflects the cut marks across that fold line.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Each fold doubles the number of layers: 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 layers. 2 circular punches across 8 layers yield 2 × 4 = 8 symmetrical punch marks upon complete unfolding.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Count total layers of paper created by the folds (2 folds = 4 layers).
Step 2: Note the location of the cut (center, perimeter, or vertex).
Step 3: Unfold in reverse sequence, reflecting cuts across each fold line to find: Eight circular punches arranged symmetrically in an octagonal pattern around the center..

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A square sheet is folded into half vertically, then folded into half horizontally.
A square hole is cut at the folded center corner (the closed vertex).
How will the paper appear when completely unfolded?
options: Four circular holes, one at each of the four outer corners
One large diamond (rhombus) shaped hole located at the exact center of the unfolded sheet.
Four circular holes forming a single small square at the center
Six circular holes arranged in two parallel columns
practiceQuestions.hint: Trace the reverse unfolding steps: each unfold reflects the cut marks across that fold line.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The folded corner corresponds to the geometric center of the sheet. Unfolding 4 layers of a corner cut around the origin forms a single composite diamond/square opening at the center.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Count total layers of paper created by the folds (2 folds = 4 layers).
Step 2: Note the location of the cut (center, perimeter, or vertex).
Step 3: Unfold in reverse sequence, reflecting cuts across each fold line to find: One large diamond (rhombus) shaped hole located at the exact center of the unfolded sheet..
